To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel method to isolate LS from the liver of the host, which we combined with a transcriptomic and proteomic approach to identify parasite genes and proteins expressed during the LS stage.
we have developed an efficient method to isolate liver-stage infected hepatocytes and used this method to perform a comprehensive transcriptome and proteomic survey of liver-stage malaria parasites.
the liver stages of malaria parasites have a distinct gene expression profile, and that a subset of proteins are expressed in the parasite liver stages only.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular processes and pathways that occur in the parasite during the liver stage of the infection and how these processes are affected by the host cell.
the identification of the proteins that are expressed during the LS stage and the pathways that are active during the LS stage.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of Plasmodium liver stage development and the identification of potential targets for intervention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying the biology of LS, and provide a foundation for future research to develop new strategies for malaria control.
the liver stages of Plasmodium are a complex and dynamic parasite stage that is essential to the completion of the parasite life cycle and the development of malaria.
we have now defined the transcriptome of the liver stages of the malaria parasite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a first attempt at a comprehensive transcriptome/proteome analysis of LS, a stage that is difficult to study in vitro and is critical in the life cycle of the parasite.
we have identified a number of proteins that are expressed during LS development that are not expressed in the blood stages and that are potential targets for drugs to treat malaria.
we have identified a large set of proteins and genes that are active during the LS of malaria parasite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the malaria parasite LS is a highly active and metabolically active stage that has the ability to produce proteins that are exported from the cell.
we were able to identify a large set of genes and proteins expressed in the LS that are likely to play a role in the biology of the parasite during this stage of the life cycle.
a combination of transcriptome and proteomic analyses can be used to identify the most important proteins and metabolic pathways in LS.
